newsitem.title: USA: EMC expects FY97 earnings,revenue growth of 25 pct.
newsitem.headline: EMC expects FY97 earnings,revenue growth of 25 pct.

text.p: EMC Corp, the Hopkinton, Mass. technology company, reported record revenues for the fourth quarter and officials expect the trend to continue.
"This year, in 1997, the plan is to achieve revenue and earnings of 25 percent," EMC President and Chief Executive Officer Michael Ruettgers said in a conference call.

The computer storage company expects to ship in volume all its Symmetrix systems this quarter adding that the six new products "completes our transition to all new models" that have lower manufacturing costs, he said.

Saying his company was the world leader in both open systems, with 15 percent of the market, and mainframe systems, with a 44 percent market share, Ruettgers expected both markets to generate revenues of more than $10 billion in 1997.
He also expects the markets to "coalesce and grow together over the next two years...we call this trend enterprise storage and this is where the market is going."
He thought EMC's Symmetrix systems, which are compatible with both open and mainframe systems, would ensure the company's dominant share in the market.
"So the hardware platforms are now paying for future software," he said, adding he was "Confident in our plan for $200 million in software revenue this year."
Ruettgers said EMC added 1,000 new customers in 1996, including Aetna Inc, Chevron Corp and Ford Motor Co in the United States, as well as Deutch Telecom.
International sales accounted for 44 percent of fourth quarter revenues and Ruettgers expected overseas sales will "increase in both absolute and percentage terms."
Revenue for the fourth quarter was $656 million, 26 percent higher than a year earlier and net income was $124 million, up 100 percent over the fourth quarter of 1995, EMC said.
